item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This guy should be Keter. He himself might be an old man, but just imagine what would happen if someone who talked with him went unnoticed. He'd infect his family and coworkers, who'd infect the people sent to deal with them, who'd infect vital infrastructure like hospitals and police. Before you know it, an entire city is in chaos!

So, either the class needs to be reassessed and containment tightened, or the ability for the "infection" to spread should be removed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, I was thinking more of where they found this guy in the first place; he came from somewhere, and his SCP-like qualities must've manifested outside of Foundation control. At some point, he was out in the wild doing what he's doing, and it would've been a while before the foundation became aware of it. Even if it was only days, hell, hours, before the foundation came in and took control of this guy, quite a few people would've been infected.

And even then, the foundation wasn't aware of the secondary contagious effects of it until after he was contained, which means during the original capture, they wouldn't have been taking in everyone who talked to him.

Basically what I guess I'm saying is; the current containment procedures are fine and pretty interesting to read, but the original capture/containment of the SCP feels like it should have a "we had to quarantine an entire town of people" in it somewhere, even if it's only mentioned in passing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, a drastic change of personality/distressed behavior is absolutely within the bounds of possibility— it's something I considered.

But so what if he did? I used to have a bit in the containment about sensors around the site perimeter, and the possible necessity of remote termination or just tranquilization, but it seemed pointless and excessive.

There's also my private canon thought that Sector-09 is only authorized to house Safe-class objects/organisms… but that's secondary to the fact that the locked box test would be literally and totally effective, in this case.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The problem is, he's human. We don't know what his behavior will be, and it's potentially catastrophic should it change (in perfectly normal, human ways) from what we've come to expect. I'm always leery of having a humanoid as safe simply because I don't believe a regular, non-anomalous human would be rightly classified as safe. The fact that this guy is ailing might push him into safe territory, but only maybe.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's not a dumb reason— but I will stop and share my own reasoning for writing it this way.

There's the implication that this SCP's effect could be Keter class. The exponential growth potential could be terrifying. But it isn't, and it never will be— precisely because it originates from a fearful, not entirely healthy or mentally vigorous 78-year-old man. He has difficulty walking to and from his own room, and is afraid to leave the building on his own. He is completely benign in personality. He probably isn't going to live much longer: as I hinted, he could be seriously injured and research staff will now think twice about sending anyone to help him.

Mentioning outright "THIS COULD GET SRS" would have been, I think, pushing the point where it doesn't need to be pushed. It's my own subjective interpretation of object classes— but I'd prefer the reader sort out why he's classed "Safe" for themselves.

item.content:encoded:
I like this one but I'm not upvoting it for the following reason, which I freely admit is a pretty dumb reason:

The sheer level of threat this guy presents isn't mentioned, really. Anyone who talks to this man will effectively go crazy within a few hours. And then anyone who talks to them will become crazy, and so on and so on. The exponential growth that could/would result from this is terrifying. It really wouldn't take long for an entire country to become afflicted, especially given the nature of it (a few hour "incubation" period, the fact that it's spread by simply talking, and the fact that there's nothing obviously horrible about the person that would stop other people from talking to them) and it somewhat bugs me that it's not brought up in the article at all.

I don't know why this particular SCP has made me think like this; there are plenty of other contagious SCPs that probably have the same issues, but it stuck out to me on this one for some reason.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My first attempt at a humanoid SCP.

Two notes:
1) The detail about living in an empty condo without realizing it is based off a story I heard in the local news— someone was literally sold a unit in an empty, maintenance-less building in Florida and lived there for weeks before realizing that something was off. Just in case I was stretching your credulity.

2) The detail about the bus stop is also true— something I heard about on NPR. It has apparently proven to be an effective means of calming patients with Alzheimer's disease at assisted living facilities, when they grow agitated and attempt to leave. They sit outside, waiting for a bus that never comes.
